title: Reranker quantization safety bands and quality acceptance matrix
creator: Ethan Wang
acceptance_criteria: Define per-slice safety bands for NDCG@10 and MRR with numeric thresholds
Calibrate INT8 and FP8 profiles and produce deterministic per-shard profiles
End-to-end evaluation harness showing <= 0.5% overall NDCG@10 regression vs FP32 baseline
No slice with > 1.0% absolute NDCG@10 degradation on slices >= 1% traffic
Automatic rollback trigger implemented in rollout pipeline for sustained >0.8% drop over 10m
Documentation and rollout runbook checked into Confluence and linked from PR
notes: Goal: create an explicit 'acceptance matrix' that maps quant profile parameters to allowed quality loss by slice and traffic tier.
Rationale: previous calibrations used single global thresholds; we need slice-aware guardrails to avoid unnoticed regressions on low-frequency but high-value slices.

Proposed safety bands: overall allowed NDCG@10 delta <= -0.5% (relative), high-traffic slices <= -0.4%, medium-traffic <= -0.7%, low-traffic <= -1.0% (absolute floor of -0.01 NDCG), MRR thresholds scaled similarly.

Calibration approach: two-stage. (1) Rapid grid sweep on representative 10k validation shard to shortlist profiles. (2) Full slice-aware evaluation across 200k queries + A/B replay for top 3 profiles.

Profile parameters to record per run: quant scheme (symmetric/asymmetric), per-layer scaling strategy, KL vs MSE calibration objective, per-channel vs per-tensor, fallback/clip thresholds, post-calib bias-correction.
We will capture stability metrics: stddev of NDCG across 5 seeds, worst-slice delta, and token-level distribution shifts for debugging.
Rollout plan: staged canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated gate checks at each step and manual signoff for any gate failures.
Observability: add per-profile telemetry to Console (route-level NDCG/MRR deltas and sample-level diffs) and integrate with alerting for sustained drift.

Operational trade-offs: FP8 gives lower latency/cost but is more brittle for rare tokens; INT8 is conservative and easier to certify. We'll target hybrid FP8 for non-embedding transformer blocks only after additional bias-correction.
Security: no customer data leaves existing pipelines; evaluation runs use mirrored internal telemetry and synthetic privacy-preserving slices for troubleshooting.
evaluation_runs: INT8 symmetric (profile A) overall NDCG@10 = 0.40905 (-0.72% rel), MRR = 0.4852 (-0.36% rel); worst-slice NDCG drop = -1.35% on tail-query slice
FP8 hybrid (profile B) overall NDCG@10 = 0.41102 (-0.24% rel), MRR = 0.4865 (-0.10% rel); worst-slice NDCG drop = -0.88%
INT8 per-channel with bias-correction (profile C) overall NDCG@10 = 0.41020 (-0.45% rel), MRR = 0.4859 (-0.22%); slice stability stddev = 0.21%
Stress-injection run: added token-noise +50% on rare tokens; profile B shows 0.6% variance increase, profile C remains within 0.3%
A/B replay (50k queries) for profile B vs FP32: uplift/decline signals: NDCG delta distribution median -0.19%, 95th percentile -0.82%
Decision so far: profile B (FP8 hybrid with conservative layer selection) is the leading candidate for limited canary pending small-slice mitigations.
